summary: Clears the existing vehicle list held in this[0..3] by destroying and freeing each node, then rebuilds it from the global vehicle array (dword_8AC390 count, dword_8AC394 base, stride 1060): one 176-byte entry per vehicle, sub-struct arrays initialized with SmallEntryStructInit, text-format reset via TextFormatStructInitializer, driver path copied via StringCopyWithBufferRealloc, setup via sub_414600, and each entry appended as a 12-byte list node to the output list.

operations.description: Walk the existing list from *this, reading each node's next pointer at +4; if the node flag byte at +8 and its data pointer at +0 are both set, destroy the payload via StructDestructor(1), then free the node via FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Zero this[0..3] (list head, tail, secondary pointer, count) after cleanup.
Read dword_8AC390 (vehicle entry count); if it is <= 0, return 1 with an empty rebuilt list.

For each vehicle entry over dword_8AC390, allocate a 176-byte entry via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper and initialize its sub-struct arrays with SmallEntryStructInit (direct calls and via sub_401000 array initializer).
Reset the text-format block of each new entry via TextFormatStructInitializer.
Copy the driver file path from vehicle+188 in the array via StringCopyWithBufferRealloc, store the current index into entry+8, and run entry setup via sub_414600(entry, 0).
Allocate a 12-byte list node via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper wrapping the entry, and append it to the output list updating head, tail, secondary pointer and count.
Return 0 after a full rebuild, or 1 when the vehicle array was empty.
